title: PRESSURE PULSATIONS AND SLAB STABILITY IN MULTI-PIPE OUTLET STILLING BASINS

PRESSURE PULSATIONS AND SLAB STABILITY IN MULTI-PIPE OUTLET STILLING BASINS

ABSTRACT

Pressure pulsations generated by hydraulic jumps can control the stability of concrete floor slabs in stilling basins. Experimental data are still scarce, however, for multi-pipe outlets that discharge into a diverging basin. To examine this case, we conducted a systematic physical modelling programme in which bottom pressure fluctuation coefficients (Cp), mean-pressure profiles, and pressure spectra were obtained from 45 experimental runs. The test matrix covered Froude numbers from 3 to 9, submergence ratios between 1.0 and 2.5, and three energy dissipator configurations under symmetric and asymmetric gate operation. Peak pulsation occurred at x/y₁ = 5–12 downstream of the hydraulic jump toe. At this location, Cp,max rose from 0.062 at Fr₁ = 5 to 0.098 at Fr₁ = 9. A regression fitted to the measurements gave the empirical relationship Cp,max = 0.0072·Fr₁1.18 (R² = 0.97). The equation is intended for hydraulic design within the tested outlet configuration. Increasing the submergence ratio from 1.0 to 1.5 lowered the peak by 18–24%. The combined toothed-sill and baffle-block arrangement produced a reduction of about 35% relative to the smooth floor. The dominant prototype frequencies lay between 0.5 and 4 Hz. This range overlaps the natural vibration range of thin concrete slabs and supports a dynamic amplification factor of 1.1 for slabs thinner than 0.25 m. Results were also compared with two prototype outlet structures in the Surkhandarya region. Slab-thickness deviations were 0.6% to 15.2%, and the mean deviation was 5.4%. This comparison supports the use of the proposed design procedure for multi-pipe outlet stilling basins.
